title: Menu-bar VM check fails intermittently, and its resize step cannot run in the macOS 27 guest
body:
## Summary

The menu-bar VM check (`task app:vm-verify-menu-bar`) fails on some runs, and its window-resize step cannot run in the current guest. Neither problem blocks 0.4.0. The delivery rule for this roadmap is that a finding blocks a release only if it breaks the happy path. These findings do not break it.

## What happened

Two separate problems showed up while the check ran on the notarised 0.4.0 bundle.

### 1. Intermittent failures

The check failed on some runs of the notarised 0.4.0 bundle and passed on others. The bundle did not change between runs (CDHash `160b0f0b39a0541f99b8d656a5c87dc3bad9ef5c`).

| Bundle | Passes | Attempts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.4.0 (notarised) | 5 | 9 |
| 0.3.0 (released) | 3 | 3 |

The last five 0.4.0 attempts all passed. The failures included these kinds:

- "the window did not come to the front". It happened twice, at different steps.
- `testanyware input move` rejected an argument of `-1` as `unexpected argument '-1' found`. It happened twice, once deep into a run.
- The resize step (see below), before the script recorded it as NOT RUN.

The sample is too small to show that 0.4.0 is worse than 0.3.0. The code difference between `v0.3.0` and the 0.4.0 commit touches no window or activation code. It touches only the workspace provider, the disclosure text, the capability catalogue and `Composition.swift`.

### 2. The resize step cannot run in this guest

In the guest (macOS 27.0.1, TestAnyware 2.7.0), a drag of the title bar or of a window corner has no effect at any position. A drag of a scroll thumb works. The same failure happens on the released 0.3.0 bundle. The cause is therefore the guest or the input tool, not Koine.

TestAnyware issue 12 covered lost input and closed in 2.7.0. It did not cover this case.

The script now probes whether the guest delivers a title-bar drag. If it does not, the script prints `NOT RUN` for the resize assertions and does not count them as a pass. It still runs the least-size screenshot and the scroll-reachability steps. The final line then says `NOT RUN, and not a pass: the resize by a drag`.

## What this means for the docs

The claim that the window resizes and keeps its content reachable rests on 0.3.0 evidence. A 0.4.0 run did not establish it again. The verification record says so.

## Open work

- Find why the window sometimes does not come to the front, and why `input move` gets `-1`.
- Report the missing title-bar drag to TestAnyware, or find a way to resize that the guest delivers.
- Take more samples on a later release to see whether the failure rate differs from 0.3.0.

Found during the `release-0-4-0-k5` grove. Roadmap: #11.
